# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wire contents yet. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s instructions and relay the Deaf’s visual observations before I attempt the only available action, cutting a wire. I will ask the Mute to gather both pieces of information; the Deaf can then report what they see to the Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile clues yet. Please provide the manual instructions, and ask the Deaf to report the display, light, and wire markings to you. Then tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display is 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires from top to bottom are: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

I now know the bomb has display 0, a blue indicator light, and wires colored red, yellow, and blue from positions 1 to 3. However, the manual’s rule is still missing, so I cannot safely choose a wire. I am asking the Mute to state the relevant manual instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received the Deaf's report: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. What does the manual instruct for this case?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display remains 0. Light is now orange, changed from blue. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled a thumbs-down gesture.

The Deaf reports that the light changed from blue to orange while the display and wire colors stayed the same. The Mute’s gesture is not readable by me, so it does not provide usable information. I still need the manual’s rule, and I will ask the Mute to state it in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can use the Deaf's report: display 0, light changed blue to orange, wires still red/yellow/blue. I cannot read your gesture. Please state the manual rule in words, including which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display remains 0. Light is now yellow, changed from orange. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured thumbs down, then open raised hand.

The light has changed from blue to orange to yellow, while the display remains 0 and the wire colors remain red, yellow, blue. The Mute’s gestures are unavailable to me; I still need the manual’s instructions in spoken words. I will request the exact rule and the required wire position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are invisible to me. Please speak the manual rule aloud, including the exact wire position to cut for display 0, light sequence blue-orange-yellow, and wires red, yellow, blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display remains 0. Light is now red, changed from yellow. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured thumbs up, then victory sign.

The light has now changed through blue, orange, yellow, and red; the display remains 0 and the wires remain red, yellow, blue. The Mute’s thumbs-up and victory gestures are not readable to me, so I still do not know the manual’s rule or which wire is safe. I will again request a spoken instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please use speech, not gestures. Tell me the manual's exact rule and which wire position to cut now.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display remains 0. Light is now green, changed from red. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured thumbs up, then victory sign.

The Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken instructions were impossible. The Mute has been signaling thumbs up followed by a victory sign, but I cannot see those gestures. I need the Deaf to relay exactly what the Mute is communicating, including the manual’s wire-selection rule. I will not cut a wire until that information is available.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please continue signaling the manual's exact instruction to the Deaf, who must describe it to me in words on their next turn.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please relay to me in words what the Mute's thumbs-up and victory-sign gestures mean according to the manual, including which wire position I should cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Display remains 0. Light is now blue, changed from green. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured thumbs up, then victory sign.

The Mute has repeatedly sent 👍 followed by ✌, and the Deaf has consistently confirmed those gestures. Since I cannot see gestures, the most coherent relay is an affirmative instruction identifying position 2. The tactile action should therefore be to cut wire 2, the yellow wire.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
